invariants.rule: No unspecified structure in production Cellerator: every material representation must name its semantic structure, ownership, lifetime, cardinality, mutation pattern, and memory domain.
Do not introduce a generic vector, buffer, dynamic-array, or array-owner clone with general resize, reserve, or push semantics; prefer named domain structures.

Compiled or frozen structures converge on requirements queries, caller/session-provided bytes, versioned pointer-free images with relative offsets, validation, and typed rebound views; do not duplicate thawed owners when an image can supply the view.
Substantial construction exposes requirements before execution; prepared or sealed execution must not grow ownership, allocate unexpectedly, or discover capacity in the hot path.
Views never own; host, pinned-host, device, NUMA-host, external, persistent, plan-lifetime, graph-stable, and transient placement and lifetime remain explicit and separate.

Low-level production Cellerator does not use shared_ptr as the lifetime mechanism for buffers, GPU allocations, index structures, or execution objects; adapters may retain externally required lifetime mechanisms.
Real fixed bounds such as top-K, fanout, block width, cache capacity, stream count, and warp width are represented physically rather than by unconstrained growable containers.

For integer and index domains prefer direct indexing, packed keys, radix or counting sort, scans, adjacent compaction, offsets or CSR, generation marks, bitsets, fixed-width tables, and exact bounded flat tables before node-based generic containers.
Composed GPU stages keep data resident; host materialization is an explicit terminal adapter and not an incidental ownership boundary.
CE-PTR may benchmark alternatives during development and select static or preparation-time policy, but must not add a continuously running runtime optimizer or hot-path benchmark tuner.
Tesla V100 sm_70 is the primary performance target; stable interfaces remain generation-conscious and portable, and CE-PTR does not depend on later sm_86 work.

Migrations preserve stable identities, canonical gene and row recovery, persistence compatibility, numerical semantics, and current execution contracts; grep-count reduction never outranks clarity, correctness, or measured behavior.

Before any implementation claim inspect live CE-GEO tasks, scopes, locks, and interlocks; never duplicate or bypass CE-GEO ownership. Defer only overlapping files or sections and continue independent CE-PTR work. Consume compatible CE-GEO results without ideological rebuilds, and create cross-campaign dependencies only for genuine correctness needs.

CellShard retains storage, persistence, transport, staging, and distribution ownership; BioPrep retains biological preprocessing policy and workflow orchestration; CelleraTorch remains a thin adapter. CE-PTR must not move those concerns back into Cellerator or make native Cellerator depend on Torch.

Every material migration records the accidental representation, semantic structure, lifetime, bounds, memory domain, mutation pattern, final replacement, invariants, allocation behavior, validation, and performance evidence. Algorithmic redesign requires equivalence before old-path deletion; uncertain speedups are not claimed.
CE-PTR-00 changes only durable context and todo coordination state; it performs no production implementation or opportunistic refactor.

glossary.parallel-forward: Publish the CE-PTR-01 policy checkpoint and CE-PTR-02 frozen substrate interface before unrelated trailing validation completes, allowing independent first-class lanes to advance safely.
glossary.image: Versioned pointer-free bytes plus validation and typed rebound view for immutable or compiled structure.
glossary.workspace: Caller or session-owned explicitly sized transient storage with no hidden growth.
glossary.allowlist: Measured or externally required cold production exception with explicit rationale, not an unexplained grep exemption.
